iucn.long: Listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List according to Wikipedia; some other sources give Near Threatened, so check the current Red List entry.

overview.text: Lataste's Viper, also called the Snub-nosed Viper, is a small viper of the Iberian Peninsula and north-western Africa. Its populations are fragmented across Portugal and Spain.

identification.text: Its most remarkable feature is the upturned tip of the snout, forming a small "nose horn" - the origin of its other name, Snub-nosed Viper.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Normally less than 60 cm; the maximum recorded total length is about 72 cm.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The Iberian Peninsula (Portugal and Spain) and north-western North Africa, including the Rif mountains of Morocco; it may now be extinct in Tunisia. The southern subspecies *V. l. gaditana* lives in the south of Portugal and Spain.

habitat.text: Rocky and scrubby country, including stone walls and sometimes coastal dunes, where its colours blend in well.

similar.text: a non-venomous water snake that copies viper patterns and behaviour; it lacks the upturned snout and is usually found in or near water.
